chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, all from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Zurara, who said:

Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: When you stand for the prayer, you must be devoted to your prayer, for only what you are devoted to is counted for you from it. And do not play with your hand, nor your head, nor your beard, nor speak to yourself, nor yawn, nor stretch, nor fold your hands, for that is what the Magians do. And do not cover your head, nor keep your feet wide apart, nor spread them like a camel spreads them, nor sit on your heels, nor stretch out your arms, nor crack your fingers, for all of that is a deficiency in the prayer.

And do not stand for the prayer sluggishly, nor drowsy, nor heavy, for these are from the traits of hypocrisy. For Allah, Glorious is He, forbade the believers from standing for the prayer while they are intoxicated—meaning the intoxication of sleep—and He said to the hypocrites: 'And when they stand up for the prayer, they stand up sluggishly; they do it only to be seen of men and (they) do not remember Allah except for a little.'

key_terms.الْمَجُوسُ: The Magians (Zoroastrians), used here as a reference for specific gestures

ai.seo_question: What are the recommended etiquettes and prohibited actions during Islamic prayer according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi details the specific physical and spiritual etiquettes of prayer, linking internal focus (iqbal) to the validity of the act while categorizing various bodily movements as deficiencies (nuqsan). It connects the physical state of the worshiper to the Quranic description of hypocrites, noting that sluggishness in prayer stems from sleepiness (sukr al-nawm) and a lack of true presence, thereby serving as a practical guide for achieving khushu'.
